evidence_summary: Contemporary advertising and later specimen research identify an early Claybridge fuzz box predating the named Fuzzmaster. The surviving pre-Fuzzmaster example matches the early company-name sticker and two-control configuration described in period ads.

Claybridge was an early Australian PA/amplifier builder that produced a documented Fuzzmaster line. Surviving research distinguishes the original Fuzzmaster, Wildcat and MKIV states; exact chronology between some states remains a research question.

Fi-Sonic, associated with Philip Dreoni, produced at least two dirt products in the 1960s. Newspaper advertisements establish a Fuzz product by September/December 1965; surviving hardware includes a distinct Fuzz Blender amp-top unit and a later Fuzz Blender MKIV pedal, while the relationship between these states remains unresolved.
Pearl Musical Instrument Co. produced the CF-1 Cry Fuzz as an early Japanese fuzz-wah product. Pearl is retained as the builder/product identity rather than assigning an OEM factory without evidence.
Pearl's later Sound Spice catalog includes DS-06 Distortion. The model is retained as a catalog lead pending stronger period documentation and factory attribution.
Pearl's later Sound Spice range includes OD-05 Overdrive. Builder identity is clear enough for discovery, while exact production corridor and OEM relationships remain to be reconciled.

The East German Trickverzerrer, also described as Böhm Trickverzerrer or simply Verzerrer, is attributed to VEB Musikelektronik in Klingenthal. The surviving evidence is sparse, so factory identity and chronology remain cautious.

marketed_identity: Cosmosound / G.I.S. / Goldsound / Gun / Meazzi and related labels
evidence_summary: Caldironi Musica in Milan is identified by specialist sources as the physical maker behind a family of Italian fuzz-wah products marketed under multiple names including G.I.S., Goldsound, Cosmosound, Gun and Meazzi. The archive treats Caldironi as the physical manufacturer and the retail names as relationship nodes.

ToneHome identifies the Goldsound Distortion Whau-Whau Repeat as a 1972/73 Caldironi Musica product also sold as Silversound SE/40 and Cosmosound Distortion Whau-Whau Repeat. This is a useful multi-brand single-manufacturer census entry.
Ricken's FR III is documented as made by JEN in Pescara, Italy, in the late 1970s. It is retained as a marketed identity under the JEN physical-manufacturer node.
